tex_content.html:
Lemma
[The Invertible Operators Are Open]

Let $E$ be a Banach space and $F$ a normed space. The set of invertible bounded linear maps $E \to F$ is open in the space of all bounded linear maps $E \to F$.

Proof

If $A_0$ is invertible, then $A \mapsto A_0^{-1} A$ is a continuous map into the bounded operators on $E$ carrying $A_0$ to the identity, and $A$ is invertible exactly when $A_0^{-1}A$ is. The units of the Banach algebra of bounded operators on $E$ form an open set, since $\mathrm{id} - T$ is invertible whenever $\| T\| < 1$, with inverse given by the convergent Neumann series $\sum _k T^k$. The claim follows by taking the preimage of that open set.

□
